text: Brisco County auditors have reported that $2.4 million in road maintenance funds was missing from county accounts after a routine review of spending from 2022 through 2024, according to a report released Tuesday. The audit found transfers to unrelated reserve accounts and several unapproved invoices that could not be matched to paving or repair work. County finance director Mara Ellison said the gaps were first flagged during year-end reconciliation and were then examined by outside accountants. “We are treating this as a serious control failure and have already frozen further transfers pending review,” Ellison said. The report recommends tighter approval procedures and a full reconstruction of the affected ledgers within 30 days.
